transcript:
This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
The Justice Department is suing more than two dozen California residents for alleged
voter crimes.
NPR's Miles Parks tells us just last week the DOJ sued the state of California and Los
Angeles County because they would not investigate the Trump administration's allegations of
non-citizens who were voting.
This all began about a week ago last Tuesday when the DOJ delivered a thumb drive to Los
Angeles County that contained the names of 20,000 people all over California who were
on the state's voter rolls and who the federal government says are likely non-citizens.
Now, I should say there are a lot of reasons to be skeptical of that number, but the DOJ
wants California to segregate the ballots of everyone on this list and for them not
to be counted until those people have been investigated.
The state says the federal government has not provided evidence for its claims and doing
what the DOJ asks would probably violate state and federal law.
NPR's Miles Parks reporting.
President Trump continues to travel the U.S., making campaign stops for Republican candidates
ahead of midterm elections in two weeks.
Trump was in Kansas last night.
He supported incumbent GOP Senator Roger Marshall.
The event was near Wichita.
Remember station K-M-U-W, Meg Britton-Melish, has more.
Because Republicans joined Trump with a message for conservative voters.
Even in deep red Kansas, the midterm races are too close to stay home.
The president lent his support to the governor's race, but made clear that his focus was on
re-electing Marshall.
And Roger Marshall is all that stands between the people of Kansas and communists controlling
the United States Senate, because if they get a couple of these people in, they're
going to have total control.
Marshall is a staunch Trump loyalist and is currently neck and neck with Democrat and
Methodist pastor Adam Hamilton.
If Democrats pick up four seats in November, they have a majority in the Senate.
For NPR News, I'm Meg Britton-Melish in Wichita, Kansas.
Italy is preparing to deploy soldiers after rioting broke out in the city of Milan.
That comes as European governments issue travel warnings for neighboring France.
Megan Williams reports.
In Milan's luxury shopping district, boutiques are emptying window displays and are boarding
up storefronts.
Protests over rising prices, low wages, and deteriorating public services erupted into
fires and looting.
Across the border in France, demonstrations over crumbling schools and the cost of living
have also turned violent, with electric bikes piled up and turned into burning barricades.
Police have imposed overnight curfews in parts of Paris, and other European governments are
warning citizens going to France to avoid demonstrations.
For NPR News, I'm Megan Williams in Rome.
And you're listening to NPR News in Washington.
The FBI, the U.S. Postal Service, and the U.S. Capitol Police are investigating dozens
of letters sent to lawmakers.
Some of the envelopes have suspicious substances they've turned up on Capitol Hill and
local congressional offices around the country.
Some state elections offices, including in Wisconsin, have also gotten them just weeks
before the midterms.
The latest envelope turned up yesterday at the local office of Virginia Democratic Congressman
Suhas Subramanyam.
There are no injuries reported.
The host of Comedy Central's The Daily Show, John Stewart, has signed a new contract.
It keeps him as host through December 2028, and Pierre's Eric Duggan's reports.
Stewart's fans will likely hear that greeting for at least a couple more years, following
news the comic will stay on as an executive producer and Monday night host, with the program's
correspondence continuing the host of The Daily Show from Tuesday to Thursday.
The Daily Show airs on Comedy Central, which is now part of the larger company Skydance,
created by Paramount's purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery.
But though critics have accused Skydance owner David Ellison of currying favor with President
Trump, an agreement to extend hosting duties by Stewart, who is a frequent Trump critic,
may help push back against that idea.
Eric Deggans, NPR News.

Trump campaigns in Wichita, Kansas, for Senator Roger Marshall ahead of midterms
